reading.body:
H.R. 7110 has 17 recorded supporters and no lobbying filings naming it, so the algorithmic bias bill is currently a party-line proposal with no registered industry engagement.

Every sponsor and cosponsor listed is a Democrat. The sponsor is Summer Lee, and the 16 cosponsors run from Eleanor Norton and Rashida Tlaib to Bennie Thompson and Frederica Wilson. A bill with support drawn entirely from one party, and no counterpart in the data, is a statement of position rather than a measure with a path to passage.

The absence of lobbying filings is the more informative fact. The summary counts zero filings from 2025 or later that name the bill, which means no registered lobbying shop has put this bill on a disclosure form. That is not the same as no industry interest. A filing that names a bill shows only that the bill was an issue in the lobbying, not what position was taken, and the absence of any filing shows only that the bill has not yet become a live enough target to be named.

The data covers the bill's sponsors, its cosponsors, its status date of 2026-01-15, and its issue tags of bias and civil rights. It does not cover the bill's text, its committee stage, any hearings, any votes, or any spending. Nothing here speaks to data centers, power procurement, or compute, and the bill's subject as tagged is model conduct rather than the physical buildout.
